title: SIGTERM is recorded and the run fails loudly; the process and the WAL are untouched

preconditions.notes: A scenario batch is running; the SIGNAL GUARD (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP) is installed, which is a runner facility and not a product code path.

timeline.detail: two writes acked, one step open

timeline.event: SIGTERM delivered to the runner process
timeline.detail: the async-signal-safe handler stores one int32 and returns; the default action never runs

timeline.event: the next long wait observes the request
timeline.detail: the run throws a reportable error naming the signal instead of letting the log stop mid-suite
one request fails one run, not every later run in the batch

notes: This fixture deliberately asserts NO durability event: SIGTERM is a runner stop request, not a persistence point, and the handler writes no WAL byte. Android must not rely on a SIGTERM handler running before a SIGKILL; the durability contract there is the same level-1 write path the kill_9 fixtures assert.
